title: Run SQL on CSV Online – Query CSV and Excel | OpenAnyDoc
description: Run SQL queries on a CSV or Excel file in your browser: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY and joins on a table named data, on your device. Free, no upload.
heading: SQL on CSV: Query a File Like a Table
subtitle: Drop a CSV or Excel file and query it with SQL as a table named data; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Run SQL on a CSV file in your browser: the file is loaded into a SQL engine on your device as a table named data, and you write SELECT queries with WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, aggregates and joins of the table with itself. Results appear in a grid and download as CSV or Excel. Excel files open their first sheet. Nothing is uploaded.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your file is opened by your own browser and never sent to a server, so nobody else sees it.

features.title: Real SQL
features.text: Queries run in a SQL engine inside the page, so standard SQL works: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, JOIN and aggregates.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: After you have used it once, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: run SQL on a CSV file

steps.title: Open your file
steps.text: Drop a CSV or Excel file, choose it, paste CSV into the paste box, or try one of the samples.

steps.title: Write a query
steps.text: Query the table named data, for example SELECT city, COUNT(*) FROM data GROUP BY city.

steps.title: Read the results
steps.text: The result appears in a grid under the query; change the query and run it again as often as you like.

steps.title: Download the result
steps.text: Save the result as a CSV or Excel file.

handles: Input: CSV files, and Excel .xlsx and .xls files (the first sheet).
Table: one table per file, named data.
Queries: SELECT with WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, aggregates and joins of data with itself (standard SQL, run in your browser).
Types: columns of numbers are stored as REAL, so sums and comparisons work on numbers.
Results: shown in a grid, downloadable as CSV or Excel.
limits: One table per file; two files can't be joined.
Standard SQL only; extensions specific to one database may not work.
Excel files: only the first sheet is loaded.
faqTitle: SQL on CSV: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The file is loaded into a SQL engine inside your browser, and queries run on your device; nothing is sent to a server.

faq.question: What is the table called?
faq.answer: data. Write queries such as SELECT * FROM data WHERE amount > 100 ORDER BY amount DESC.

faq.question: Which SQL dialect is used?
faq.answer: Standard SQL, run by a SQL engine in your browser. SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, aggregates such as COUNT, SUM and AVG, and joins of the table with itself all work.

faq.question: Can I join two CSV files?
faq.answer: No. Each file is one table named data, so joins are only of that table with itself.

faq.question: Can I query an Excel file?
faq.answer: Yes. Its first sheet is loaded as the table data.

faq.question: How are number columns typed?
faq.answer: A column of numbers is stored as REAL, so SUM, AVG and comparisons such as amount > 100 treat its values as numbers, not text.

faq.question: How do I query a CSV file with SQL?
faq.answer: Load the CSV into a SQL engine as a table and run SELECT queries on it, the same way you would query a database. In OpenAnyDoc, open the CSV and write a query such as SELECT * FROM data WHERE amount > 100; it runs in your browser without uploading the file, and the results download as CSV or Excel.
